speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. You mentioned persistent vomiting and chest pain; to help me understand your condition, have you noticed if the pain gets worse when you take a deep breath or move your upper body?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture).

Given the history of forceful vomiting following heavy alcohol consumption, followed by a choking episode and sudden chest pain, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of an esophageal perforation. I am proceeding to order a water-soluble contrast esophagram to confirm the diagnosis and assess the extent of the leak.
